general_information.Description: This specialization is developed for seniors and fresh graduate students to understand fundamental network architecture concepts and their impacts on cyber security, to develop skills and techniques required for network protocol design, and prepare for a future of constant change through exposure to network design alternatives. Students will require a prior knowledge of C programming, an understanding of math probability and a computer science background is a plus.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Student must get the certification of Computer Communication specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination. 2. Complete the online course to be allowed to take Final Exam
general_information.Note: 1. Final Exam is included of Final Theory Exam (TE) & Final Practical Exam (PE): 100% 2. Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded. 3. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & Final PE Score >=4 & FR >= 5 (FR = min(10, (Final TE Score + Final PE Score)/2 + bonus)

description: This specialization is developed for seniors and fresh graduate students to understand fundamental network architecture concepts and their impacts on cyber security, to develop skills and techniques required for network protocol design, and prepare for a future of constant change through exposure to network design alternatives. Students will require a prior knowledge of C programming, an understanding of math probability and a computer science background is a plus.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Trace the evolution of networks and identify the key concepts and functions that form the basis for layered architecture
Explain fundamental concepts in digital communication, and focus on error control techniques that include parity check, polynomial code, and Internet checksum
Describe peer-to-peer protocols and local area networks, how does a peer-to-peer protocol deliver reliable data transfer service across unreliable transmission lines or networks

Describe how medium access control protocols coordinate the access to the communication channel so that information gets through from a source to a destination in the same broadcast local area network
Describe packet networks from two perspectives, concerned with services that the network provides to the transport layer that operates above it at the end systems
Describe addressing and routing procedures, as well as congestion control inside the network.
Explaine how IP enables communications across a collection of networks, hierarchical structure of IP addresses and explain their role in ensuring scalability of the Internet
Explain role of address prefixes and the uses of masks, TCP three-way handshake, flow control, and congestion control, Multicast, SDN and security
